rulings.evidence: Exact vocabulary match; the different-form flag is only a breasts/breast token artifact. EACH-WEIGHT is the real ruling: 4 x 8 oz (227 g), because a breast must be big enough to pocket, and the check validates it at 63 g protein/serving against the source's 61 (the Chicken Florentine cutlet error in reverse).

'To taste' with no quantity, so the 1 tsp salt booked here is MY estimate for four stuffed breasts, with the matching black pepper on the buy string. Marked optional to preserve the source's own framing.

REUSE, NOT a new id - and this one nearly went the other way. The board search reported no commodity for the phrase, but mozzarella-cheese is live on the everyday board with captured part-skim shredded cells at Walmart, Kroger, Hy-Vee, Aldi, Our Family and Sam's Club. NOT reduced-fat-mozzarella (70 vs 304 cal per equal weight) and not the Daiya vegan shreds.

REUSE: parmesan is a live 7 of 7 id with grated-cheese cells at every store, and Parmesan Cheese is an existing label row. Only the vocabulary row is missing, which is a naming question and not a registrar one. 1/3 cup grated = 33 g.

rulings.raw: ½ teaspoon EACH: dried basil, dried oregano
rulings.evidence: Composite line booked on dried oregano (1 tsp = 1 g); the matching 1/2 tsp dried basil rides the buy string uncosted at about 0.5 g. Both are explicitly dried, so there is no fresh flip to adjudicate.

macro_cross_check.verdict: PASS, cleanly, on all three figures - protein within 3.3%, carbohydrate within 1 g, calories 7.2% under. That agreement is what validates the 8 oz each-weight on the main protein line: at the catalog-average 167 g the dish would fall about 12 g of protein short of the source, and at a 6 oz breast it would miss the calorie floor logic entirely. Comfortably inside both run conditions (519 cal, 9 g carb).
